transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Reyes (Northstar Head of Platform), Marcus Lee (Eng Manager), Priya Shah (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Quick discovery on integration approach; customer mostly interested in Redwood hosted initially but needs private options for PCI-scope workloads.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'll let liam introduce himself and then we can hear about northstar's goals?
00:12 Liam: hi all, liam chen, solutions engineer. quick agenda: integration touchpoints (sdks, langchain/llamaindex), networking (gateway/proxy, vpc), quotas/rate limits, observability hooks and next steps.
00:25 Olivia: thanks, maya, we run core payments fraud and reconciliation services. evaluating llm features for customer support and internal summarization first. goal is low latency for chat (under 300ms ideally) and strict pci scoping — some workflows must be private.
00:45 Maya: helpful. curious what your current stack looks like — languages, orchestration, and any langchain usage already?
00:55 Marcus: mostly python microservices on k8s, we use fastapi. we have a small langchain prototype in a sandbox for ticket summarization; it's using the openai connector but we want to switch to something self-hosted or hosted provider with better control and cost.
01:12 Priya: from infra side, we need VPC peering or private link, sso via okta, key management in our KMS, and audit logs. SOC2 is a checkbox. also we have bursty traffic — days with spikes at EOD and monthly reconciliation windows.
01:35 Liam: makes sense. on integrations: Redwood provides python/js SDKs with a simple client. we also have LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters — sample code that plugs into chains and retrievers. our adapter set includes streaming support and chunked embeddings.
01:55 Olivia: quick question: is the LlamaIndex adapter maintained upstream? i've seen different forks; do you have an official one?
02:05 Liam: we maintain official examples and a maintained adapter in our repo — note: in transcription that's 'LamaIndex' in some docs, but repo is LlamaIndex. i'll share the repo link after the call. it includes examples for embeddings, vector store wiring, and a retriever that uses redwood embeddings endpoint.
02:30 Maya: important to mention hosted vs dedicated vs private: hosted is easiest (api key, sdk), dedicated gives you reserved capacity & predictable latency SLAs, private gives the VPC/on-prem controls you need for PCI. each has slightly different network setup and onboarding time.
02:50 Marcus: how different are the sdk endpoints between hosted and dedicated? we want minimal code changes if we switch later.
03:00 Liam: same SDK interface and routes; config points (api_host, api_key) change. we try to keep client interface identical so you can swap by changing base url and credentials. some advanced features like private network endpoints and KMS integration require extra config.
03:20 Olivia: on rate limits — we have both steady realtime traffic for chat and large async jobs for monthly reports. how do quotas work? can we set per-team or per-route limits?
03:32 Liam: yes, per-route quotas, per-api-key quotas, and per-customer caps for dedicated. there are burst windows and token-based accounting. you can configure throttling behavior — queue vs reject — and set soft vs hard limits. we'll also expose metrics for throttles in the console.
04:00 Priya: do you expose request ids / tracing headers so we can correlate with our tracing (jaeger/datadog)?
04:08 Liam: yes — every response includes x-redwood-request-id and we support distributed tracing headers (traceparent). we also have per-route telemetry in the console with token/latency breakdowns; you can stream logs to our log forwarder or push them to your splunk/datadog via the observability hooks.
04:35 Marcus: for embeddings — we want local vector stores (we use qdrant) with LlamaIndex. how does embedding throughput and rate-limiting look?
04:45 Liam: embeddings are accounted per-embedding unit. we have bulk endpoints with batching and concurrent upload guidelines. for high throughput we'll recommend dedicated capacity and intelligent batching settings; also caching of prefixes/embeddings at your side helps.
05:05 Olivia: network egress — can we have an IP allowlist or private link? some of our PCI subnet can't route to the public internet.
05:15 Liam: yes you can request dedicated private endpoints with VPC peering or private link. private deployments provide customer-managed control plane options if you need on-prem.
05:30 Priya: KMS question: does Redwood support customer-managed keys? our security team won't allow plaintext tokens stored in vendor KMS in some cases.
05:40 Maya: we support KMS/HSM integrations for dedicated and private. hosted customers can use our managed KMS but for PCI workloads we often recommend dedicated with your KMS integration or private deployment. i'll include a security doc that details how keys are handled.
06:05 Marcus: any gotchas around model selection and latency? we run sequences of about 512 tokens typically.
06:15 Liam: kernel and compilation selection impacts latency. we pick optimized kernels for model arch and seq length. for 512 tokens, choose models with verified perf profiles; we can share perf numbers. also quantized variants trade quality for cost/latency — we'll help recommend profiles via Redwood Optimize.
06:40 Olivia: do you have a pricing example for chat usage vs embeddings? rough ballpark.
06:50 Maya: i'll send a pricing matrix. hosted is pay-as-you-go; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; private is enterprise license. i'll attach an example with per-1k-token and per-embedding-unit numbers.
07:05 Priya: onboarding timeline — how long to get dedicated capacity?
07:12 Liam: depends — hosted you can go live same day; dedicated typically 4-6 weeks for provisioning and capacity planning; private (VPC/on-prem) is 6-12+ weeks depending on network and compliance work.
07:30 Olivia: we might start with hosted for non-PCI workflows and move to dedicated/private for PCI-scope. is that a common path?
07:40 Maya: very common. many customers start hosted for experiments then upgrade to dedicated for predictable economics, then private for compliance-sensitive workloads. SDK compatibility is designed to minimize changes.
07:55 Marcus: observability hooks — can we get per-prompt latency breakdowns and token-level cost per request?
08:05 Liam: yes, we have token-level cost/latency breakdowns in console and you can export traces and raw logs. per-prompt breakdowns are available when you enable verbose tracing on the route; beware of cost/retention tradeoffs.
08:25 Priya: is there a way to throttle particular endpoints to preserve capacity during bursts?
08:30 Liam: yes — per-route throttles and fairshare policies. you can also set fallback policies to a cheaper model variant automatically when capacity is constrained.
08:45 Olivia: about function calling and structured outputs — we use tools and function-like calls in our chains. any special handling?
08:55 Liam: we support streaming with partial function call payloads and structured output enforcement. some transcriptions may show 'function call' text, but it's native in the API. we also have schema validation features.
09:15 Maya: quick clarification on LangChain/LlamaIndex support — Liam will send examples. any specific adapters you need?
09:22 Marcus: LlamaIndex -> qdrant connector + local caching; LangChain -> retrieval-augmented-generation with streaming. also examples for prompt templates and rate-limiter middleware.
09:35 Liam: noted. we'll include middleware examples and a small demo repo.
09:45 Olivia: security audits — do you provide SOC2 report and pen test summary?
09:50 Maya: yes, SOC2 report, ISO where applicable, and we can sign an NDA and provide pen test summary. for dedicated/private we can provide more detailed infra diagrams and audit logs. link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (will send post-call).
10:15 Priya: traffic pattern — we have a baseline of ~20 req/s for chat and spikes to 200 req/s during batch windows. also monthly heavy embedding job at ~1M items. how do you recommend piloting?
10:30 Liam: recommend a 2-week pilot: spin up hosted test routes with your sample traffic, run perf tests, collect telemetry, then scope dedicated if needed for the embedding job. for the 1M items, consider bulk endpoints + batching or ephemeral dedicated capacity.
10:50 Marcus: any caching options to reduce token costs?
10:55 Liam: prefix caching, KV cache for dialogs, and embedding dedupe caching. Redwood Optimize can recommend cache and quantization profiles based on sample workload.
11:15 Olivia: ok next steps then — send pricing, security docs, and the langchain/llamaindex repo. schedule pilot kick-off.
11:30 Maya: recap: we'll send pricing + security doc (maya), liam will send integration examples, customer to share traffic profile and allowlist. aim to reconvene for pilot kick-off next week.

Links shared: Redwood LangChain examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples (shared after call)
Security one-pager: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (to be emailed)

End of transcript.
